questions.questionText: A farmer can produce both beef and lamb. The opportunity cost of a kilo of beef is three kilos of lamb. The price of a kilo of beef is twice that of lamb. What should he do if his aim is to maximise his revenue?

options.A: concentrate on beef production
options.C: produce beef and lamb in the ratio 3:2
options.D: produce twice as much beef as lamb

questions.questionText: What advantage do banknotes (paper money) have over coins (metallic money)?

options.A: They are cheaper to produce.
options.B: They are more useful for low value transactions.
options.C: They are the only form of legal tender.

options.A: the consumer surplus derived by the individual from the last unit consumed
options.B: the equilibrium price of the good
options.C: the quantity demanded by the individual at any given price
options.D: the value of the individual’s marginal benefit from the last unit consumed

options.A: by aggregating the supply of all firms producing the product
options.B: by averaging the supply of all firms producing the product
options.C: by calculating the supply of the typical firm producing the product
options.D: by estimating the supply of the largest firm producing the product

A consumer needed a new camera and a new armchair. She was prepared to spend $500 on one item. She discovered that the camera cost $450 and the armchair $500. She bought the camera. What was her opportunity cost and her consumer surplus? opportunity consumer cost surplus

options.A: the armchair $50

questions.questionText: In which set of circumstances will prices play no part in determining how resources are allocated between alternative uses but may still have a role as a rationing mechanism?

options.A: The government sets maximum prices for all goods above their market clearing price.
options.B: The government sets minimum wages for all workers below the market rates of pay.
options.C: The quantities of consumer goods produced are determined by the government.
options.D: The total income consumers have available to spend is fixed by the government.

options.A: demerit good

options.A: consumers landlords employers

questions.questionText: A country joins a trade organisation, where the only requirements are that members must have identical tariff rates towards non-members and no trade barriers to fellow members. With which possible change in status for the country is this condition consistent?

options.A: from independent trade to membership of a free trade area
options.B: from membership of a customs union to membership of an economic union
options.C: from membership of a free trade area to membership of a customs union
options.D: from membership of a free trade area to membership of an economic union

questions.questionText: In Australia in 2005 a shipload of exported iron ore paid for 2200 imported flatscreen TVs. In 2010 the same size shipload paid for 22 000 imported flatscreen TVs. Which combination of price changes is certain to cause this change in the terms of trade of Australia? average export price average import price

options.A: decrease decrease

questions.questionText: A country has a population of 500 million. 15 million people are unemployed and the country has an unemployment rate of 6%. What is the size of the labour force?

options.A: 90 million B 250 million C 470 million D 485 million

options.A: boom in consumer spending

questions.questionText: What would increase both demand-pull and cost-push inflation?

options.A: an appreciation of a country’s currency
options.B: an increase in the cost of borrowing
options.C: an increase in the level of its import tariffs
options.D: an increase in the price of oil

questions.questionText: A UK resident buys shares in a Spanish company. What will be the immediate and subsequent effects on the UK’s balance of payments? immediate effect subsequent effect on financial account on current account

options.A: credit credit
